script_data.title: The Pudding Cup Millionaire
script_data.description: A civil engineer turns discounted pudding into a lifetime of free flights with a brilliant loophole.
script_data.script:
In the early 2000s, David Phillips was your archetypal mild-mannered civil engineer from California. Meticulous by trade, he possessed an extraordinary eye for detail that would soon turn a mundane grocery trip into a legendary tale of ingenuity. His life was about to take an unexpected detour, not through new highway bypasses, but across continents.

One ordinary afternoon, while browsing the frozen aisle, Phillips noticed a promotion on Healthy Choice pudding cups: "Get 500 frequent flyer miles for every 10 UPC barcodes submitted." Most people would shrug, perhaps collect a few hundred miles. David saw something else entirely – a blueprint for unlimited travel. He immediately did the math. A typical frequent flyer mile cost around 2 cents. Healthy Choice puddings were on a deep discount, sometimes as low as 25 cents per cup.

His brilliant loophole was this: 10 cups for $2.50 (if each was 25 cents) yielded 500 miles. That meant he was acquiring miles for just half a cent each! But he didn't stop there. He realized he could buy thousands of these discounted puddings, donate the food to charity, and claim a tax write-off for the full retail value of the donated goods. This effectively made his miles acquisition almost free, or in some scenarios, even a net profit.

Execution required precision. Phillips didn't just buy a few dozen. He drove to every major supermarket in the area, negotiating to buy out their entire stock of Healthy Choice puddings. He ended up purchasing 12,150 individual pudding cups, spending a total of $3,149. His home, briefly, transformed into a mini-warehouse of dessert. With his family's help, he meticulously peeled off all 12,150 UPC labels, which he then mailed to Healthy Choice. The puddings themselves? They were loaded into a truck and delivered to the Salvation Army and other food banks, providing meals to those in need, and securing Phillips a significant tax deduction.

Healthy Choice, and eventually Continental Airlines (who partnered with the promotion), were stunned when a single submission arrived with thousands of UPCs, but the promotion had no limits. David Phillips had legitimately earned 1.25 million frequent flyer miles. This audacious, harmless caper not only earned him lifetime elite status but allowed him and his family to circumnavigate the globe multiple times, experiencing first-class travel for virtually free. It’s a spectacular reminder that sometimes, the greatest adventures begin with a closer look at the fine print.

script_data.used_topic_seed: Uncover the incredible true story of David Phillips, a civil engineer who turned a mundane grocery store promotion into a lifetime of free flights. By meticulously calculating and executing a brilliant loophole, he transformed thousands of pudding cups into millions of frequent flyer miles.
